facts.text: Ozone earned its name from the fresh, thunderstorm‑after air that early settlers called “ozone,” a term still celebrated by local postmistress Delia McCracken.
The community sits in the heart of the Ozark National Forest, about 15 miles north of Interstate 40, making it a hidden gem for scenic drives.
Though it closed in 1957, the Ozone School remains a much loved community landmark that still echoes the town’s educational past.
Interpretive trails in Ozone highlight Civilian Conservation Corps history, blending education with exploration for hikers and history buffs alike.
Motorcyclists frequent Ozone for its sweeping curves and ever‑changing vistas along the scenic byway, making it a popular stop for riders.
Ozone Burger Barn stands as one of the area’s rare retail establishments, offering a unique culinary stop amid the forest’s tranquility.
